findings.title: Team admins and owners are checked with AND
findings.body: This requires the caller to be both a team admin and a team owner. Those are separate team roles, so an admin or owner who is not also in the other role is rejected by the permission check and cannot add guests. This should authorize either role.

findings.title: Guest blacklist can be bypassed with uppercase addresses
findings.body: The blacklist entries are lowercased, but `guest` is compared without normalization. Since email validation accepts uppercase addresses, a caller can submit a differently cased version of a blacklisted address and have it added as a guest. Normalize both sides before checking the blacklist.

findings.title: The server accepts duplicate guest addresses
findings.body: This schema validates each address but does not require the array to contain unique addresses. The uniqueness check exists only in the dialog, so a direct tRPC request can submit the same address multiple times; the handler does not deduplicate those entries before `createMany`, potentially creating duplicate attendees or causing the mutation to fail on a database constraint.

findings.title: Email notifications use the unfiltered guest list
findings.body: The handler filters out guests who are already attendees before inserting them, but passes the original `guests` array to the email sender. If a caller includes an existing attendee while adding a new guest, the sender classifies that existing attendee as newly added and sends them a scheduled-booking invitation instead of the existing-attendee notification. Pass the filtered list to the sender.

findings.title: Calendar sync failure leaves attendees added but unnotified
findings.body: The attendee rows are committed by the preceding booking update before this external calendar update runs. If calendar synchronization throws, the mutation exits before sending emails, while the new attendees remain in the database. The user sees a failure, and retrying can fail because those addresses are now already present, leaving them without invitations. Handle this partial-success case or arrange the flow so it can be retried safely.
